title: Shockwave traffic jams recreated for first time
summary: A one-minute New Scientist clip showing a Japanese experiment in which drivers on a circular track produce a spontaneous traffic jam that travels backward. It illustrates phantom traffic jams without any obstacle.
why: It is the go-to demonstration HN links whenever traffic shockwaves, phantom jams or cascading failures come up.

quote.text: They told 22 drivers to drive in a circular path at 30 km/h. A traffic jam appeared, and moved backward.
